name: io.github.neilberkman/clippy
title: Clippy - Smart macOS Clipboard Tool
description: Copy AI-generated content to the macOS clipboard, including Gmail-ready rich email drafts, text, code, files, and recent downloads.

tools.name: clipboard_copy
tools.description: Copy plain text or files to clipboard. Use 'text' for generated plain content, 'file' for one file reference, or 'files' for multiple file references. For a drafted email that should paste into Gmail with formatting, use the dedicated copy_email tool instead.

text.description: Plain text content to copy. For a formatted email draft, use copy_email.

file.description: File path to copy as a single file reference

files.description: List of file paths to copy as multiple file references in a single clipboard operation

force_text.description: Set to 'true' to force copying file content as text (only valid with 'file')

tools.name: copy_email
tools.description: Copy an email to the macOS clipboard as high-fidelity Gmail-ready rich text. Prefer the structured salutation, body_markdown, and signoff fields so spacing and line breaks are explicit and language-independent. The legacy markdown field accepts a complete Markdown body. A normal Command-V paste preserves intentional paragraph spacing, bold, italic, links, lists, inline code, and Mimestream-style fenced code blocks. HTML, RTF, and plain-text fallbacks are provided for compatibility. This tool only copies content; it never addresses or sends email.

markdown.description: Complete email body in Markdown (legacy compatibility form). Do not combine with the structured fields.

salutation.description: Opening salutation, kept tight against the body

body_markdown.description: Email body in Markdown; use with salutation and signoff for explicit structure

signoff.description: Closing and signature; newlines are preserved

tools.name: copy_slack
tools.description: Copy CommonMark/GFM Markdown to the macOS clipboard as a native Slack message, preserving bold, italic, strike, inline code, code blocks, lists, quotes, and links. Prefer this over clipboard_copy for Slack; it never sends or posts. Input is Markdown, not Slack mrkdwn: use **bold** and ~~strike~~. For multiline code or aligned columns, put triple-backtick fences on their own lines with real newlines, and pad columns with spaces inside the fence. Content indentation is preserved but is not required for a code block. Markdown pipe tables become unaligned text rows, not monospaced tables. Set expected_code_blocks when intending code blocks (e.g. 1 for one fenced table); a mismatch fails before copying. Use preview=true to inspect formatting counts and warnings without changing the clipboard. Success confirms copying, not Slack's rendering. Paste with normal Command-V. Plain-text clipboard reads omit formatting and fence markers; they cannot verify Slack formatting. If reported code blocks are correct but the paste is wrong, investigate the clipboard/paste path instead of removing fences or switching to plain-text copy. The md2slack CLI uses the same renderer.

markdown.description:
Message in CommonMark/GFM Markdown. Code block example (newlines between each line): Before

```
  name   value
  alpha  10
```

After. Fence only the code/table, not the entire message. Preserve existing padding when editing.

preview.description: Render and report formatting counts and warnings without changing the clipboard (default false). This is not a visual preview of a Slack paste.

expected_code_blocks.description: Expected number of rendered code blocks (non-negative integer). Set this when intending code blocks, such as 1 for one fenced table. A mismatch returns an error and leaves the clipboard unchanged; omitted means no count check.

tools.name: clipboard_paste
tools.description: Paste clipboard content to file or directory. Intelligently handles both text content and file references from clipboard.

tools.name: get_recent_downloads
tools.description: Get list of recently added files from Downloads, Desktop, and Documents folders.

tools.name: buffer_copy
tools.description: Copy file bytes to agent's private buffer. Reads actual file bytes (no token generation). Supports line ranges for precise refactoring. Agent never touches or regenerates the copied content.

start_line.description: Starting line number (1-indexed, omit for entire file)

end_line.description: Ending line number (inclusive, omit for entire file)

tools.name: buffer_cut
tools.description: Cut lines from file to buffer - copies to buffer then deletes from source. Like buffer_copy but removes the lines after copying. Use for moving code sections without manual deletion. Atomic operation - only deletes if copy succeeds.

start_line.description: Starting line number (1-indexed, omit for entire file)

end_line.description: Ending line number (inclusive, omit for entire file)

tools.name: buffer_paste
tools.description: Paste file bytes from agent's buffer to file. Writes exact bytes without agent token generation. Supports append/insert/replace modes for surgical refactoring.

to_line.description: End line for replace mode (inclusive, required for replace)

tools.name: buffer_list
tools.description: Show what's currently in the agent's buffer (metadata only, not content).

prompts.name: copy-recent-download
prompts.description: Copy the most recent download to clipboard

arguments.name: count
arguments.description: Number of recent downloads to copy

prompts.name: paste-here
prompts.description: Paste clipboard content to current directory

examples.description: Generate code and put it directly on your clipboard

examples.description: Use copy_email to put the Markdown draft on the clipboard as Gmail-ready rich text
